bifrost: std::sync primitives used directly (springboard/sdk/src/dispatch.rs, springboard/render/src/purgeable.rs); no SDK wrapper module
summary: Apple's framework is a set of low-level Swift primitives: typed atomics, a lazy atomic reference, a closure-scoped Mutex and memory-ordering enums. BifrOSt apps are Rust and use the std equivalents directly; the SDK has no wrapper module for these and no WordPair equivalent.

features.apple: Atomic<Value> with add, bitwiseAnd, load, store, exchange, compareExchange (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/synchronization/atomic)
features.note: Rust std atomics only; no SDK-level wrapper or documented SDK API for atomics
std OnceLock covers the one-time init case; no atomic-reference type for arbitrary strong references

features.apple: WordPair, a pair of two word-sized UInts stored atomically (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/synchronization/wordpair)
features.note: grep for WordPair and pair-atomic wrappers in springboard/sdk, ui, render and core returned nothing
Swift protocol mechanism for storing custom types atomically; Rust uses the fixed std atomic types, so there is no counterpart to expose
std::sync::atomic::Ordering used directly; no per-operation ordering type in an SDK API
std fence is available to Rust code; no SDK function or documented use found

features.apple: Mutex<Value> with init, withLock and withLockIfAvailable (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/synchronization/mutex)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/dispatch.rs:24 (lock helper over std::sync::Mutex), springboard/sdk/src/dispatch.rs:250 (static JOBS Mutex)
features.note: std Mutex used widely; the closure-scoped withLock and withLockIfAvailable shape is not offered as an SDK type

gaps: No SDK wrapper for Mutex with closure-scoped withLock and withLockIfAvailable; apps use std::sync::Mutex guards directly
No WordPair or double-word atomic in the SDK or the UI, render or core crates
No SDK-level atomic wrapper or documented memory-ordering API; apps reach std::sync::atomic directly
No atomic reference type equivalent to AtomicLazyReference beyond std OnceLock
